title: Safety, precision and repeat trials
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:22Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank point only covers repeat trials, averages and repeatability versus reproducibility, while the new point is broader and also needs risk management for safety and choosing equipment for precise measurements.

draft.title: Safety, precision and repeat trials
card: Before an investigation, spot what could cause harm and plan how to reduce it. This might mean wearing safety glasses, tying back long hair or using a heatproof mat.

A precise measurement has very small steps and gives close results each time. Choose equipment with a scale that suits the job. A measuring cylinder with 1 mL marks is more precise than a cup with 50 mL marks.
A repeat trial runs the same test again in the same way. If the results are close each time, they can be reproduced, so we can trust them more.
One result may be a fluke or a slip. Several trials let you find the average and see how much the results vary.
draft.remember: Plan for risks, pick equipment that suits the measurement, and repeat trials to check results.

a.q: Why does a student repeat the same trial three times?
opts: To see whether the results can be reproduced
To make the equipment more precise
To remove the need to manage risks
To change the independent variable each time
a.why: Repeating a trial shows whether similar results come up again. It does not change the equipment, so it cannot make the equipment more precise.
a.clue: Think about what close results each time would tell you.

b.q: Priya times how long a toy car takes to roll down a 2 m ramp, about 1.5 seconds. Which choice gives the most precise timing?
opts: A stopwatch that reads to 0.01 s
A wall clock with only a minute hand
A stopwatch that reads to 1 s
A watch with a second hand marked every 5 s
b.why: A stopwatch reading to 0.01 s has the smallest steps, so it can show small differences in a short time. The 1 s stopwatch is tempting because it is a stopwatch, but its steps are too large for a 1.5 s roll.
b.clue: Pick the scale with the smallest steps for a short time.

a.best: To see whether the results can be reproduced

b.best: A stopwatch that reads to 0.01 s
